changedBeliefs: Exp 229's suggestion that SIMD JSON escape scan is a real TEXT-side mechanism is confirmed only for very long safe spans. The final AArch64/NEON fused classify-and-copy prototype improves the 1 KiB safe ASCII lane -33.6% / -34.1% and the CJK lane -25.2% / -25.5% across the order flip.

The practical break-even row is not strong enough to ship. Safe ASCII at 256 B improves -17.7% then -12.6%, missing the predeclared >=15% floor in the second ordering. A vector kernel can be compelling at 1 KiB while still failing the representative lower boundary where per-cell dispatch/setup is a material share.

Unsafe handling is the load-bearing design constraint. A speculative SIMD copy followed by scalar restart regressed a late escape at 96 B by 15-26%. Continuing scalar from the first unsafe vector and dispatching only TEXT >=256 B removed that double pass: early-escape 256 B moved +2.7% / -0.9% and late-escape 256 B improved -16.0% / -5.8%. The final runtime is still rejected and archived at `archive/exp-230` because the safe 256 B gate failed.
nextSignals: Keep the portable SWAR scan + copy implementation as the canonical JSON TEXT encoder. Do not retry another length threshold, in-function NEON body, or speculative-copy-and-full-restart variant under the current workload.

Keep `benchmark/experiments/select_bytes_text_string_reserve.dart` as the durable TEXT encoder gate. Future work must include safe 64/96/256 B and 1 KiB/CJK lanes, plus early- and late-escape guards at both sides of its proposed cutoff. The exact long-string `dart:convert` oracle in `test/native_encoder_diff_test.dart` is the byte-identity gate.

Reopen fused SIMD classification-and-copy only with a production/AOT profile showing escape-free TEXT >=1 KiB materially dominates result-transfer wall, or a different mechanism that removes the 256 B dispatch/setup floor. The archived prototype demonstrates the reachable large-span ceiling without obligating runtime complexity.
